production.malt: FEW describes its whiskeys as grain-to-glass and made from locally sourced grains; its bourbon uses a high-rye three-grain recipe and its rye combines a high rye content with corn.
production.fermentation: FEW states that its bourbon fermentation uses a saison-style yeast, contributing spicy and fruity fermentation character.
production.maturation: Its bourbon is matured in charred oak barrels and its rye in air-dried oak barrels.

houseCharacter: FEW's public technical disclosure emphasises grain selection, yeast choice and small-batch maturation rather than detailed still geometry. The use of saison-style yeast in bourbon fermentation is a distinctive flavour-building choice that supports spicy and fruity character before maturation. High-rye recipes and charred or air-dried oak then reinforce a robust American whiskey profile.
cask23Narrative: FEW Spirits is an Evanston distillery whose technical identity is built around local grain, small-batch production and an unusually expressive fermentation choice: saison-style yeast in its bourbon. That yeast contributes another layer of spice and fruit before the whiskey meets oak, while the high-rye grain structure keeps the spirit lively and assertive. It is a useful American comparison for customers who want to see how yeast selection can matter as much as mash bill and barrel char.
